title: Two Coworkers Talk About Replying to Messages on Time
script: Citra: [curious] Reza, can I ask you something? How do you reply on time without checking work messages all night?
Reza: [thoughtful] Ha, it's a habit my old manager taught me. She said important work messages need a timely reply, but people also need clear working hours.
Citra: I never really thought about it that way. I usually just reply whenever I feel like it.
Reza: [gently] I understand that, but imagine someone waiting for an answer because they need it to finish their own work.
Citra: [regretfully] That's true. Last week, I left a client waiting for three days because I completely forgot to check my messages.
Reza: [practically] That happens to everyone sometimes, but During working hours, I send a short acknowledgement if I cannot answer fully. After hours, only our emergency channel alerts me.
Citra: What do you usually write when you are too busy to answer properly?
Reza: [warmly] Something simple, like, thank you for your message, I will answer properly by tomorrow. It only takes ten seconds to type.
Citra: I never thought a quick reply like that could matter so much to someone.
Reza: [reflective] It does, because silence makes people feel ignored, even if you did not mean to ignore them at all.
Citra: Do you also have rules about how you write your replies to people?
Reza: [carefully] Yes, actually. I always read the message twice before answering, so I do not misunderstand what they need from me.
Citra: That's smart. I sometimes reply too fast and give the wrong answer, then I have to correct myself later.
Reza: [firmly] Exactly, so speed matters, but understanding matters even more. Adab in messages means being both prompt and thoughtful.
Citra: I think I have been careless about this for a long time. I want to change that starting today.
Reza: [encouraging] Start with a clear response time, use an emergency channel, and do not promise a deadline you cannot keep.
Citra: Thank you, Reza. I am going to reply to that client right now, even though it is three days late.
Reza: [lightly] Better late than never. Good luck with the reply!

quiz.question: What is Citra curious about?
options: How to write to friends at midnight
How Reza replies promptly without working all night
quiz.explanation: The revised opening focuses on both responsiveness and boundaries.

quiz.question: What did Reza’s manager teach?
options: Every message requires an immediate answer
Reply time and working-hour expectations should be clear
quiz.explanation: Timeliness does not require permanent availability.

quiz.question: What problem did Citra create last week?
options: A client waited three days without an update
She sent a reply too early
She answered the wrong client immediately
quiz.explanation: Forgetting the message left another person unable to plan.

quiz.question: What does Reza send when a full answer is not ready?
options: A promise to answer in ten seconds
A short acknowledgement with a realistic response time
quiz.explanation: A brief update manages expectations honestly.

quiz.question: What matters more than speed alone?
quiz.explanation: A quick wrong reply creates more work.

quiz.question: What protects Reza’s personal time?
options: He turns every device off permanently
Only an emergency channel alerts him after hours
He answers all messages before sleep
quiz.explanation: Urgent needs have a defined route without making every message urgent.

quiz.question: What does an “acknowledgement” do?
options: Confirms receipt before the complete answer
Moves the message to another company
quiz.explanation: It tells the sender that the message was seen and sets an expectation.

quiz.question: Why does Reza read a message twice?
options: To make the message sound urgent

quiz.question: Which promise would follow Reza’s advice?
options: I have read this but cannot explain when
I will confirm the figures by 3 p.m. tomorrow
quiz.explanation: A specific realistic time is both prompt and honest.

quiz.question: What broader balance defines message adab?
options: Respecting another person’s work and one’s own boundaries
Treating every request as an emergency
quiz.explanation: The revised dialogue combines care, clarity, and sustainable availability.
